sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for saved model checks
sections.what: Imports the JSON tools, the error type, the ingestion and model steps, and the saved model structure.
sections.why: Lets the tests load and check saved model files directly.

sections.name: _model_json
sections.title: Build a model and return its JSON
sections.what: Ingests the sample schedule into a temporary database, builds the BRIDGE-B project model, checks it has components, and returns it as plain JSON data.
sections.why: Gives the other tests a real saved model to change and reload, instead of a made-up one.
sections.watch_out: The project ID BRIDGE-B must exist in the sample file, or this helper fails first.

sections.name: test_new_models_do_not_gain_compatibility_fields
sections.title: New models carry no compatibility fields
sections.what: Checks that a freshly built model has no specification revision, no specification overrides and no old wbs_paths field on any component.
sections.why: Likely reason: those fields belong only to older or newer versions, so new files should stay clean and not carry them.
sections.watch_out: Adding one of these fields back to new models would make this test fail on purpose.

sections.name: test_later_version_fields_load_and_round_trip
sections.title: Newer fields load and save again
sections.what: Adds a component wbs_paths list and a specification revision of 0 with empty overrides to the saved model, loads it, and checks the paths survive loading and saving.
sections.why: Likely reason: an older app must still open files written by a newer version without losing the extra data.
sections.watch_out: The test assumes the loader keeps unknown-to-this-version fields rather than dropping them.

sections.name: test_unapplied_specification_edits_are_refused
sections.title: Refuse unapplied edits from newer versions
sections.what: Sets a specification revision of 2 with a rating override, then checks that loading fails with an error that says the file came from a newer Schedule3D version.
sections.why: Likely reason: this version cannot apply edits it does not understand, so loading them would silently produce a wrong model.
sections.watch_out: The error text match is exact, so changing the message breaks the test.

summary: Checks that saved project models stay readable across app versions: new models do not gain old compatibility fields, newer saved fields load and round-trip, and unapplied specification edits from a newer version are refused.
purpose: Protects saved model files so that a newer or older Schedule3D version can open them without losing or inventing data.
why: Likely reason: users keep saved models for a long time, so the app must read files written by a later version without damage.
how: A helper builds a model from the sample multi-project CSV and returns its JSON. One test checks that the new model has no compatibility fields. Another adds newer fields, loads the model and checks it round-trips unchanged. The last adds unapplied specification edits and expects an error that mentions a newer version.
inputs: The sample file samples/sample-multi-project.csv and temporary database files.
outputs: Pass or fail results. The tests write only temporary files.
risks: The newer-version refusal depends on the exact error text. The tests rely on the sample containing the BRIDGE-B project and at least one component.
debug: If the tests fail, compare the JSON from the _model_json helper with the fields the test expects. For refusal failures, check the validation message wording and the specification revision value.
